checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is Uint.from_be_bytes offset parsing in extract_deposit_data protected against integer overflow?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate all implementations of extract_deposit_data across Go, Rust, and Java clients. 2. Identify the Uint.from_be_bytes (or equivalent) calls that parse offset values from deposit data. 3. Verify that the parsed offset value is explicitly bounds-checked BEFORE being used in any comparison or arithmetic operation. 4. Test with maximum uint values (0xFFFFFFFF for 32-bit, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF for 64-bit) to trigger potential overflow. 5. Test with offset values that would cause the sum (offset + length) to overflow. 6. Verify that implementations reject malformed deposits with out-of-bounds offsets rather than wrapping around. 7. Check if safe math libraries or checked arithmetic operations are used for offset calculations.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0036, Trust Boundary: tb-002, Subgraph: SG-001. This is a critical pre-condition for safely parsing deposit data from the deposit contract. An attacker could craft a malicious deposit transaction via P2P or direct transaction submission that causes the offset parsing to overflow, potentially leading to memory corruption, out-of-bounds reads, or incorrect deposit processing.

checklist.title: Verify Bounds Check Order: Are offset value bounds checks performed BEFORE comparison operations in extract_deposit_data?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the control flow of extract_deposit_data to map the exact sequence of operations. 2. Identify where the parsed offset is first compared or used arithmetically. 3. Verify that explicit bounds checking (offset <= MAX_SAFE_VALUE) occurs BEFORE any comparison that could overflow. 4. Check for implicit truncation when casting between integer sizes (e.g., uint64 to uint32). 5. Construct a test case where offset = MAX_INT - small_value, and verify proper rejection. 6. Verify that the bounds check uses less-than-or-equal rather than less-than to prevent off-by-one errors at boundaries.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0036, Pre-condition verification. The order of operations matters: if comparison happens before bounds checking, an attacker could exploit the overflow window. This check verifies the defensive programming pattern is correctly implemented.

checklist.title: Verify Cross-Client Consistency: Do all Ethereum client implementations handle offset overflow identically?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the extract_deposit_data implementation in each major client: Geth (Go), Lighthouse/Reth (Rust), Besu/Teku (Java). 2. Create a standardized test vector with edge-case offset values (MAX_INT, MAX_INT-1, 0, negative equivalents in signed contexts). 3. Execute the same malformed deposit data against each client implementation. 4. Verify all clients either accept or reject the deposit identically - consensus-critical. 5. Document any behavioral differences that could lead to chain splits. 6. Check language-specific overflow behavior: Go panics vs Rust checked_add vs Java ArithmeticException.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0036, Trust Boundary: tb-002, Actors: actor-deposit-contract, actor-el-node. Inconsistent handling of overflow across clients could cause consensus failures where some nodes accept a deposit and others reject it, potentially enabling chain splits or deposit theft.

checklist.title: Is the requests hash computation in compute_requests_hash deterministic across all inputs and execution contexts?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the compute_requests_hash function implementation and all call sites. 2. Verify that the SHA-256 digest computation uses a fixed, canonical serialization format for the input requests_list. 3. Check for any sources of non-determinism: (a) ordering dependencies - ensure input list is processed in a consistent order, (b) floating-point operations that could vary across platforms, (c) pointer-based ordering or memory addresses in serialization, (d) timestamp or random number injection, (e) uninitialized memory reads. 4. Create test cases with identical input lists and verify byte-for-byte identical output digests across multiple invocations. 5. Test edge cases: empty list, single-element list, maximum-size list, lists with duplicate elements. 6. Verify determinism across EL-CL node boundary (tb-004) - both actor-el-node and actor-cl-node must produce identical hashes for identical inputs. 7. Check that hash computation is not affected by global state or mutable singletons.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to violate the invariant by: (1) Providing the same requests_list in different orders and checking if different hashes are produced, (2) Calling compute_requests_hash from different execution contexts (threads, processes) with identical inputs, (3) Injecting subtle variations in the input encoding that should normalize to the same logical input, (4) Testing across system restarts to check for state-dependent behavior.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Type: Invariant, Security Goal: SG-003, Trust Boundary: tb-004. This is a CRITICAL property because non-deterministic hash computation at the EL-CL boundary could cause consensus failures, chain splits, or enable manipulation of block validity checks.

checklist.title: Verify Cross-Client Determinism: Do all Ethereum client implementations compute identical requests hashes for the same input?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Create a comprehensive test vector set with various requests_list inputs (empty, single request, multiple requests, maximum size). 2. Execute compute_requests_hash against each major client implementation: Geth (Go), Lighthouse/Reth (Rust), Besu/Teku (Java), Nethermind (C#). 3. Compare SHA-256 digests byte-for-byte across all implementations. 4. Verify that the serialization format for requests is identically interpreted (SSZ encoding, length prefixes, field ordering). 5. Test with requests containing maximum-size fields and boundary values. 6. Document any discrepancies - even a single bit difference is a consensus-critical bug. 7. Verify that EL and CL components within each client also produce identical hashes.
checklist.falsification_approach: Attempt to find inputs where different client implementations produce different hashes by: (1) Testing edge cases in SSZ serialization, (2) Testing handling of optional/nullable fields, (3) Testing unicode normalization if any string fields exist, (4) Testing endianness assumptions in multi-byte integer encoding.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Type: Invariant, Security Goal: SG-003, Trust Boundary: tb-004. Cross-client consensus is critical for network stability. Any deviation in hash computation could cause chain splits where nodes running different clients disagree on block validity.
